__readme: This file drives the GUI of the Room Config Builder. Edit it and press
'Reload Schema' in App Config (or restart the app) - no compile needed.
Each entry under 'fields' is keyed by a config.json property name and supports:
label:       Field label shown in the editor (defaults to the raw key).
labelWhen:   Condition -> label overrides, checked against the OTHER keys
in the same config block; the first match wins and none
matching falls back to 'label'. Conditions are 'key=value'
(equals) or 'key~text' (contains), case-insensitive. Used by
both the editor and the device report - e.g. input_usb reads
'VGA' when gui_usb_or_vga is VGA.
description: Text behind the (i) info button.
helperText:  Small grey hint line under the field.
type:        auto | text | int | double | bool | dropdown | combo | hidden | module_states.
'auto' (default) infers from the JSON value type.
options:     For dropdown/combo. Plain strings, or objects with value/label.
writes:      For combo only - the list of config keys the one dropdown writes.
Combo options use 'values' (one entry per key in 'writes').
moduleCommand: For module_states only - the command in the device's Python
module whose states become the options. Parsed live from the
module's self.Commands dictionary ('AllowedValues'), falling
back to the Set<Command> / __Match<Command> ValueStateValues.
addIfMissing: render the field on a device tab even when the key does not
exist in that device block yet; the first edit writes it into
config.json. Works on a 'fields' entry (every device tab, as
serial_port uses) and on a 'device_fields' one (only the
matching family). Device tabs only - the System tab draws
exactly the keys the block holds.
hideWhen:    List of conditions (same 'key=value' / 'key~text' form as
labelWhen) that make the key IRRELEVANT to this block. Any one
matching and the field is not drawn, the key is not added to a
new device, Check Defaults does not offer it, and applying a
module's DEVICE_INFO defaults skips it - so serial_port and
baud never reach a Network or SerialOverEthernet device, which
reaches its hardware by ip_address + net_port instead. Changing
the gating value (com_type) in the editor REMOVES the keys that
just became irrelevant, and says so in the log.
Keys may contain '*' wildcards (e.g. 'power1_outlet_*') to cover a whole
family of properties. Exact keys always win over wildcard matches.
Keys starting with '__' are ignored (use them for comments).
DEVICE-TYPE SCOPING: the top-level 'device_fields' object holds entries that
apply ONLY to matching config sections, keyed by a section pattern like
'PROJECTORDEVICE_*'. Scoped entries override the global 'fields' entries for
those device tabs - so a projector-only setting (or a projector-specific take
on a shared key like 'input') ships by editing this file, no recompile.
DEVICE DEFAULTS: the top-level 'device_defaults' object maps section patterns
to property/value pairs merged into every NEWLY CREATED device block of that
type (when the Setup Wizard counts change). Existing/template values are
never overwritten - only missing keys are added. Exact section names (e.g.
'SWITCHERDEVICE_1') override wildcard patterns per property, so switcher 1
can carry the audio groups while extra switchers stay clean.
DEVICE TYPES: the top-level 'device_types' object lists the device families
the Setup Wizard manages - each SYSTEM_SETUP dev_ count key mapped to its
section 'prefix' (required) and wizard 'label'. This list REPLACES the
built-in one, so keep every family you want here; the order here is the
wizard's display order. Adding an entry gives the new family a wizard count
dropdown, device tabs, export pruning, count audits, and a '0' default on
load. Pair it with 'fields'/'device_fields' entries for its properties and
'device_defaults' for its baseline values. Optional per-family extras:
max:                 highest count the wizard offers (default 8).
keepAlivePreference: command names tried in order when auto-picking a
new device's keep_alive_command from its module.
template:            full block for new devices when the config has no
<PREFIX>1 block to copy (else a basic one is built).
SYSTEM DEFAULTS: the top-level 'system_defaults' object holds the
SYSTEM_SETUP values injected into loaded configs that are missing them
(the migration step). Defining it REPLACES the built-in set. The dev_
counts are NOT listed here - every device_types family is always
injected as '0' automatically.
RUNTIME KEYS: the top-level 'runtime_written' list names config items the
PROCESSOR maintains itself while the room runs (the power schedule times,
ENVIRONMENT.traceback_allowed). A downloaded config carries them even
though the template never did, so they are skipped by the template audit
and are not drawn as unknown keys. Entries are 'SECTION' or 'SECTION.key'
with '*' wildcards.
CONSISTENCY: the top-level 'consistency' list cross-checks keys that have
to agree - when one condition holds, another must too. Violations never
block an edit or a save; they paint the red mismatch outline on every
field the rule flags so the tech can see both sides and fix the wrong one.
See the '__readme' inside that list for the entry format.
STANDALONE SECTIONS: config blocks that are neither SYSTEM_SETUP nor a
numbered device (e.g. 'METRICS_CONFIG') are rendered on the System tab as
their own group, below System Settings. Describe their properties under
the top-level 'section_fields' object (same entries as 'fields', keyed by
section name), give the group its heading with a normal 'fields' entry
named after the section, and list the baseline properties under
'section_defaults' - those are created/filled on load just like the
SYSTEM_SETUP migration, and are what 'Check Defaults' offers for the
group when the template config has no such block.
The wizard's device families. 'prefix' is the config section prefix the
numbered blocks use (PROJECTORDEVICE_1, ...); 'label' is the wizard text.
'max' caps the wizard count dropdown. 'keepAlivePreference' lists the
keep-alive commands to try (in order) when a new device's module is
parsed; if none match, 'Power'-style commands are used as before.
'systemKeys' lists SYSTEM_SETUP key patterns ('*' wildcard) that only
mean anything while the family has hardware in the room - setting its
wizard count to 0 removes them, so a room with no power controller
carries no outlet names. Same rule the key_map.json 'removals' entry
applies when an existing config is loaded.

dev_projectors.label: Projectors / Displays
dev_projectors.__comment: 13, not 8: a share room (active_share_room) drives a wall of panels off one grid page and the processor builds ProjectorHandler_1..13 for it. Slots 1-4 are the only ones with a projector detail page.

dev_nav_switchers.label: NAV Stream Managers
dev_nav_switchers.__comment: AV-over-IP stream managers (NAVigator), deliberately NOT part of dev_switchers: SwitcherManager sends its handlers Set("Input", ...) and reads temperature off them, and a NAVigator answers none of that. It is a matrix of encoders and decoders only NavShareManager knows how to tie, so it has its own family and its own count. The room-wide share_* keys below are its systemKeys - dropping the count to 0 takes them with it.

dev_share_stations.label: Share Stations (NAV)
dev_share_stations.__comment: The student-station displays on a NAV share room's share page. Each one is an encoder input and a decoder output on the NAVigator, and is usually reached serially over its own SP device (com_type SPI's cousin: com_type Serial with 'host' set to an spdevice<n> alias). Its per-station SYSTEM_SETUP keys are the systemKeys below, so a room that is not a NAV share room carries none of them.

__readme: SYSTEM_SETUP values injected on load when missing (shown in the
acknowledgement dialog). Edit values here and press Reload Schema.
Whole non-device config blocks injected on load when missing (section
and/or individual properties), shown in the acknowledgement dialog.
ENVIRONMENT lists controlscript_profile ONLY: every room has to declare
which ControlScript build the processor runs, so a conversion writes
'pro' and the tech switches the Xi rooms over on the System tab.
traceback_allowed is deliberately still absent - it is opt-in per room,
so a conversion never turns it on (the strip in app_state.dart is the
other half of that). Add it by hand when a room needs it - the device
report then states that it is allowed.
METRICS_CONFIG ships enabled with the bearer token filled in, so every
converted room reports metrics without a follow-up edit. The token is
what makes that safe: the processor's Metrics client raises at startup
when 'enabled' is true and 'bearer' is empty, so never blank the bearer
while leaving 'enabled' true. New configs built from the template get
the template's own values instead.

runtime_written: __readme: Config items the PROCESSOR writes into config.json while the room runs, so a downloaded file carries them even though the template never did. Listed here they are not reported by the template audit and not drawn as unknown keys on the System tab. Entries are SECTION or SECTION.key; * matches any run of characters.

__readme: Which input_* keys a room is entitled to, given the sources it has.
'tokens' maps one piece of gui_tab_type (DOC_USB_WL -> DOC, USB, WL) to
the switcher-input key that source needs. 'always' are the keys every
layout carries, plus the ones some OTHER setting governs (the extended
desktop input, the sub switcher's input). 'cameras' only exist while
dev_cameras is above zero.
Anything present but not entitled is removed, and put back if the tab
type or the camera count brings it back. Only keys named here are ever
touched, so an input_ key the schema does not know about is left alone.
Cross-key checks: when 'when' holds in a section, 'expect' must hold
too, or every field named in 'flag' gets the red mismatch outline and
'message' as its helper line. Conditions are 'key=value' (equals) or
'key~text' (contains), case-insensitive; '{key}' in a message inserts
that key's live value. Optional 'section' (default SYSTEM_SETUP)
accepts a '*' wildcard. Nothing is blocked or auto-corrected - the
tech sees both fields flagged and decides which one is wrong.
Entries without 'when' and 'expect' are skipped, which is what lets
this comment sit in the list. Defining any rule here REPLACES the
built-in set, so keep every rule you want in this array.

consistency.message: Sources include VGA (gui_tab_type is "{gui_tab_type}") but gui_usb_or_vga is "{gui_usb_or_vga}" — set it to VGA, or pick a USB sources option.
Sources include USB (gui_tab_type is "{gui_tab_type}") but gui_usb_or_vga is "{gui_usb_or_vga}" — set it to USB, or pick a VGA sources option.

__readme: Baseline properties per device type, applied when the wizard creates the
blocks. Edit the values here and press Reload Schema - no recompile.
Field definitions scoped to one device type. The outer key is a pattern
matched against the config section name (e.g. PROJECTORDEVICE_1); the
inner entries use exactly the same properties as 'fields' above.
A key defined here as well as in 'fields' takes ITS addIfMissing from
here - which is how use_device_mute is offered on the screens and
nowhere else.

use_device_mute.description: Whether pressing Video Mute also mutes the PICTURE at this display itself. Only asked here: PROJECTORDEVICE_* is the family that covers both projectors and flat panels (see device_role), and nothing else in a room has a picture of its own to blank. Not to be confused with speaker_mute, which is the same idea for the display's SPEAKERS.

input.label: Input
input.description: Input the projector subscribe status follows. The options are read live from the selected Python module's 'Input' command dictionary, so only states that module actually supports are offered (manual typing still allowed). In a share room this is the COMBINED-mode input — the leg of the room's distribution that reaches this screen — and input_individual is what it shows in individual mode.

device_role.label: Device Role (device_role)

options.label: (auto — decide from the model list)
projector (lamp hours, detail page, box-power relay)
display (flat panel — no lamp hours, no relay)

device_role.helperText: Blank falls back to the processor's display-model list
device_role.description: Whether this slot is a flat panel or a lamp projector. The processor asks that question in three places — whether to read lamp hours, whether to build a box-power relay, and whether the panel says 'Display' or 'Projector' — and this key answers all three at once. Left blank it falls back to the processor's display-model list, which is demonstrably incomplete (the Sharp PN-C603D and PN-LE601 are panels and are not on it), so set it explicitly on anything the list gets wrong. An unrecognised value is logged and falls back to the list.

input_individual.label: Individual-Mode Input (input_individual)
input_individual.helperText: SHARE ROOMS ONLY — leave blank and this screen is not a station
input_individual.description: The station's own local input (usually HDMI 1), shown when a share room is switched to individual mode; 'input' is what the same screen shows in combined mode. Setting this is what MAKES a screen a station: leave it blank and the screen keeps one configured input and holds it, exactly as every non-share room's displays already do. The room-wide Combined/Individual toggle on the grid page drives every station at once, and share_room_default_mode picks which one the room starts in.

speaker_mute.label: Mute Device Speakers (speaker_mute)
speaker_mute.helperText: Absent from a config the processor treats as ON — turn it off to leave this display's audio alone
speaker_mute.description: Whether the room's audio mute also silences THIS display's own speakers. On (the processor's default when the key is absent) it mutes them with the display's own commands — the mute state, or a volume of 0, whichever speaker_mute_method selects. Turn it OFF for a display that IS the room's audio output, or for a room whose audio is routed and controlled at the switcher/DSP instead, where the program mute already happens on that device and the display should be left alone. Not the same as use_device_mute, which hands VIDEO muting to the display's AV mute / shutter; this key is only ever about its speakers.

speaker_mute_method.label: Speaker Mute Method (speaker_mute_method)

options.label: volume (set the device's volume to 0)
mute (send the device's mute state)

speaker_mute_method.description: How the display's speakers are silenced. 'volume' (default) calls the module's volume command with 0; 'mute' sends the module's mute state (AudioMute / SpeakerMute / Mute — whichever that driver exposes). Volume is the default because a muted display usually parks a MUTE banner on screen and leaves it there. A module with no volume command falls back to its mute command on its own, and one with neither is skipped rather than guessed at.

speaker_unmute_volume.label: Speaker Unmute Volume (speaker_unmute_volume)
speaker_unmute_volume.helperText: Only read when the method is 'volume'. Blank/absent = unmute with the mute command instead
speaker_unmute_volume.description: The level restored when unmuting a display that was silenced by volume: setting a volume to 0 does not record what it replaced, so there is nothing to go back to without this. Left unset, the processor unmutes with the module's mute command rather than pick a number that could be far too loud in an empty room. Note that 0 is a real level here and would leave the room silent — clear the key (trash button) instead of typing 0 if you want the fallback.

default_input.label: Default Input (default_input)

options.label: 1 (the room PC / first host)
2 (the laptop plate / second host)

default_input.helperText: The input the room sits on. The morning restart toggles away from it and back
default_input.description: Which host the USB switcher hands the room's camera and microphone to when nobody has chosen. The processor drives this input once at startup, and the morning restart toggles to the OTHER input and back to force the USB devices to re-enumerate — so this is what the room comes up on every day. Only 1 and 2 are accepted: these are two-input switchers, and the processor logs a warning and falls back to 1 for anything else. Set it to 2 in a room wired with the laptop plate on the first port.

__readme: Field definitions for standalone (non-device) config blocks, keyed by
section name. Same entry format as 'fields'; these win over the global
'fields' entries inside that section, so short property names like
'enabled' or 'uri' can be described per block without colliding.
Only the properties present in the block are rendered - the optional
tuning keys below are described here so they get a proper editor when
someone adds them by hand in the Raw JSON tab.

enabled.label: Metrics Enabled (enabled)
enabled.helperText: Needs a URI and a bearer token before it is turned on
enabled.description: Start the python metrics client (modules/project/metrics_client.py) on the processor. When false, a no-op DummyMetrics stands in and nothing is sent. WARNING: with this true and 'bearer' blank, the processor raises at startup - fill in the URI and token first.

keylogger.label: Log UI Events (keylogger)
keylogger.description: Send a metric for most touch panel events (button presses and the like) on top of the system's own metrics. Button releases and slider drags are skipped by the processor for performance.

uri.label: Metrics Ingest URI (uri)
uri.description: Full URL the processor POSTs batched metrics to, e.g. http://cts-metrics1:41796/metrics. Points at the AV-System-Metrics ingest service.

bearer.label: Bearer Token (bearer)
bearer.description: Secret sent as the 'Authorization: Bearer ...' header on every metrics POST. The ingest service rejects the batch without it, and the client refuses to start when it is blank.

batch_size.description: OPTIONAL. Metrics are sent once this many are queued (processor default 20). Also the maximum number sent per request.

flush_interval.description: OPTIONAL. Seconds to wait before sending a partial batch (processor default 10), so a quiet room still reports.

max_cache_size.description: OPTIONAL. Most metrics held in memory while the ingest server is unreachable (processor default 250). Must be >= batch_size. Oldest entries are dropped only once the failure thresholds below are passed.

failure_drop_message_threshold.description: OPTIONAL. Failed messages tolerated before the cache is allowed to drop its oldest entries (processor default 100).

failure_drop_time_threshold.description: OPTIONAL. Seconds of continuous send failures before the cache is allowed to drop its oldest entries (processor default 300).

request_timeout.description: OPTIONAL. Seconds to wait on the HTTP POST before treating it as failed (processor default 10).

send_heartbeat.description: OPTIONAL. Send the periodic 'Heartbeat' metric used to track room uptime (processor default true).

controlscript_profile.label: ControlScript Profile (controlscript_profile)
controlscript_profile.description: Which ControlScript build the processor runs: 'pro' for an IPCP Pro, 'xi' for an Xi. Every converted room gets 'pro' - switch it here when the room is on Xi hardware, since the processor reads this to pick the right runtime behaviour.

traceback_allowed.label: Allow Tracebacks (traceback_allowed)
traceback_allowed.description: Let the processor report full Python tracebacks when something raises, instead of swallowing the detail. Opt-in per room: a conversion never adds it, and the device report calls the setting out whenever the room does carry it.

morning_power_on_time.label: Morning Power-On Time (morning_power_on_time)
morning_power_on_time.description: Set by the PROCESSOR, not by hand: the time it next brings the room up, written back into config.json as the schedule shifts. Shown here for reference — editing it is overwritten on the next cycle.

nightly_shutdown_time.label: Nightly Shutdown Time (nightly_shutdown_time)
nightly_shutdown_time.description: Set by the PROCESSOR, not by hand: the time it next shuts the room down, written back into config.json as the schedule shifts. Shown here for reference — editing it is overwritten on the next cycle.

btn_name.description: GUI object name for the connection status that has two states. Usually represented as a red dot when disconnected.

com_type.description: Type of connection as a string. 'Serial' opens a COM port on the host processor/spdevice (the only one that reads serial_port and baud); 'SerialOverEthernet' and 'Network' both reach the device by ip_address + net_port; 'HTTP' posts to it over ip_address + net_port with the user/password credentials; 'SPI' reaches the device over the Extron SP bus, where the host alias IS the address and there is nothing else to give.

host.description: The processor or spdevice in use for serial connections. On an SPI device it is the whole address: 'host' has to name an spdevice<n> alias from SYSTEM_SETUP, and the processor logs a warning and falls back to processor1 for anything else.

relay_host.description: The processor in use for the relay power control.

__comment: The two halves of a device's connection, each gated by 'hideWhen' on
com_type and each 'addIfMissing' so the fields the device DOES need
are always on its tab, whether or not the block carries them yet:
Serial only     serial_port, baud
Network / SoE   ip_address, net_port, protocol, service_port,
user, password
SPI             NEITHER half. An Extron SP bus device (a NAVigator)
is addressed by 'host' alone - the spdevice<n> alias
IS the address - so it is the one connection with no
port, no socket and no credential to fill in.
Switching com_type in the editor removes whichever set just became
irrelevant, and key_map.json applies the same split on conversion.
'host' is on neither list - it names the processor/spdevice a serial
line is wired to and is harmless (ignored) on a network device.

device_id.description: The ID to be sent to the device if it is required. Shown where a block already carries one, or where the model's driver asks for one — not offered on every device, because almost none of them need it.

gve_id.description: String that identifies the device in GVE. Needs to be created when you add the room devices to GVE.

input.description: Input for the device. The subscribe status will change to this input. (Examples: HDBaseT, HDMI 1, Digital Link).

ip_address.description: IP address for the device as a string. Network, SerialOverEthernet and HTTP all reach the device through it; a Serial device is wired to a COM port on its host instead and does not carry the key, and an SPI device is addressed by its spdevice alias alone.

keep_alive_command.description: Command as a string to send to the device once connected. Chosen from the dictionary of commands in the module.

keep_alive_interval.description: Timing for sending the keep_alive_command as an integer.

keep_alive_qualifier.description: Only needed if the command requires a qualifier (Example checking an audio group such as '1' as the qualifier).

lbl_name.description: Name for the GUI object that will be written for connection status.

manual_disconnect.description: Flag to disconnect the item. Used if a projector or item is temporarily removed from a room.

model.description: Model of the device. Picking a model from the dropdown switches 'module' to that model's default python file and applies the module's DEVICE_INFO connection + standard defaults (protocol, port, keep-alive, input, ...). The list is built from each module's DEVICE_INFO "models" list (falling back to its self.Models keys) and is filtered to this tab's device family via DEVICE_INFO "device_type"; the browse dialog can show all types.

keep_alive_trigger.description: Delay the keep_alive_command until the trigger is received such as the APC needing to complete the login before polling.

default_cc_aud_cam.description: In a two-camera room, start with the AUDIENCE camera selected as the capture-card source instead of the instructor camera — what the far end of a call sees when the room comes up. Ignored in a room with fewer than two cameras.

gui_capture_source_available.description: Whether the panel offers a capture-source page at all — the controls that pick what gets sent to the capture card / USB interface for a Zoom or Teams call. 'No' hides them, for a room whose capture feed is fixed or that has no capture card.

gui_usb_or_vga.description: Set the GUI and metrics to send over the USB or VGA depending on the age of the room.

ntp_primary.description: Network Time Protocol (NTP) primary server address in use for the processor.

ntp_secondary.description: Network Time Protocol (NTP) secondary server address in use for the processor.

output_audio_ald.description: Switcher output feeding the Assisted Listening system. It gets the same audio tie as output_audio on every source change and at startup, so the ALD hears whatever the room hears. Blank in a room without one. Non-digits are stripped, so '4A' reaches the switcher as 4.

gui_demo_mode.description: Bring the room up with every device faked: each one gets a dummy connection handler, so the panel is fully usable while nothing is actually talked to. For demonstrating or exercising a panel off the hardware. Leave it false in a live room — no command reaches a device while it is on.

module.description: File path to the module as a string.

name.description: Name of the device as it will appear in the logger.

net_port.description: Network Port used to send communications on network connected devices. Not carried by a Serial device, which talks over serial_port at the baud rate instead, nor by an SPI device, which has no socket at all.

protocol.description: Protocol in use for network connections (TCP, SSH, or UDP). SSH is what makes the processor send user + password as credentials on connect. Not carried by a Serial or SPI device.

serial_port.description: Serial port in use if using Serial as the com type (e.g. COM1). Only the Serial connection opens a port on the host — a Network or SerialOverEthernet device reaches its hardware by ip_address + net_port, and an SPI device by its spdevice alias, so the field is not offered and the key is not written for those.

baud.label: Baud Rate (baud)
baud.description: Line speed of the serial connection, passed to the processor's SerialInterface when the port is opened (default 9600). Match whatever the device's own RS-232 settings say. Serial-only, like serial_port.

service_port.description: Port for the response from the device. 0 is automatically assigned by the processor. Not carried by a Serial or SPI device — the processor has no service port to open for a COM line or an SP bus.

use_device_mute.description: Whether pressing Video Mute also mutes the PICTURE at this display itself — the processor sends the module's AV mute / video mute / shutter command on top of muting the switcher output feeding it. Turn it on for a display that must black out even when it isn't fed from the switcher, or one whose own blanking is cleaner than dropping the signal. Not to be confused with speaker_mute, which is the same idea for the display's SPEAKERS.

user.description: Username for the device when using a network connection. Sent as a credential on an SSH or HTTP connection, and pushed into the module's deviceUsername on a plain TCP/UDP one when the driver has that field. Not carried by a Serial or SPI device.

password.description: Password in use while using a network connection that requires authentication. Paired with 'user' — see that key for how each connection sends it. Not carried by a Serial or SPI device.

__comment: The individual group_ entries were removed: the 'group_*' wildcard
further down covers every audio group key (DSP and switcher alike)
with one description. Add an exact group_ entry back only when one
key needs its own label/description/type.

processor1.description: Device alias for import from the room's Extron json file. These can be used to set the host on serial devices.

processor2.description: Device alias for import from the room's Extron json file. These can be used to set the host on serial devices.

spdevice1.description: Device alias for import from the room's Extron json file. These can be used to set the host on serial devices.

spdevice2.description: Device alias for import from the room's Extron json file. These can be used to set the host on serial devices.

spdevice*.helperText: Blank = the alias is not in this room; the processor skips it
spdevice*.description: Device alias for an Extron SP device (an SP bus expander, a NAVigator, an eBUS panel), matching the name in the room's Extron json file. A device names one of these in its 'host' to say which box its COM port is on — a share room's station displays are each on COM1 of their own SP device, which is why the aliases run past spdevice2. It is also the whole address of a com_type 'SPI' device. A blank alias is skipped by the processor rather than built, so the unused ones cost nothing.
spdevice*.__comment: Wildcard fallback covering spdevice3 upward; the exact spdevice1/spdevice2 entries above still win.

active_debug_server.description: Run the processor's debug server, so a debug client can attach to the running room and watch its logs live. Nothing to do with the inactivity timer. The reboot listener (active_reboot_listener) is separate and works with this switched off.

active_event_space.description: Put the room on the EVENT inactivity timer — 6 hours before it shuts itself down, against the normal 3. For a room that regularly hosts long sessions with no touch panel activity. The room's Timer button cycles normal / event / disabled and writes the choice back into config.json on the processor; disable_inactivity_timer (25hrs) outranks this flag.

active_notifications.description: Send the room's Teams notifications (device offline, system errors) to the teams_webhook URL. The panel can toggle this at runtime and the processor saves the new value back into config.json.

disable_inactivity_timer.label: Disable Inactivity Timer (disable_inactivity_timer)
disable_inactivity_timer.helperText: Not a true disable - it pushes the shutdown out to 25hrs
disable_inactivity_timer.description: Selects the 'disabled' inactivity mode: the warning/shutdown timers move out past a full day (25hrs) so a multi-day event is never shut down on the presenter. Works with active_event_space (normal 3hr / event 6hr / disabled 25hr); this flag wins. The room's Timer button cycles the modes and saves both flags back into config.json on the processor.

use_qos.label: Use QoS Scheduler (use_qos)
use_qos.description: Route device Set/Update traffic through the quality of service scheduler (modules/project/quality_of_service.py) instead of firing every command the moment it is raised. Commands are queued by priority (high / low / lossy) and drained on a 100ms tick, so bursts of polling cannot starve what the user just pressed. False sends everything immediately, as older systems did.

active_reboot_listener.label: Reboot Listener (active_reboot_listener)
active_reboot_listener.description: Run the standalone TCP reboot listener (modules/project/reboot_listener.py) so the CTS Dashboard - or anything that can open a socket - can reboot the processor and the touch panels. Independent of active_debug_server: it has its own port and runs with the debug server switched off. False skips the listener entirely and the room can only be rebooted on site.

reboot_listener_port.label: Reboot Listener Port (reboot_listener_port)
reboot_listener_port.description: TCP port the reboot listener binds. Must not collide with the debug server or any other service on the processor. The CTS Dashboard has to be pointed at this port.

reboot_listener_interface.label: Reboot Listener Interface (reboot_listener_interface)
reboot_listener_interface.description: Which processor network interface the reboot listener binds to. Keep it on LAN unless the dashboard reaches the processor over the AV LAN.

reboot_listener_token.label: Reboot Listener Token (reboot_listener_token)
reboot_listener_token.helperText: Blank = no token check; set one for anything off a trusted VLAN
reboot_listener_token.description: Shared secret required in front of every plain-text command line (e.g. '<token> reboot processor'), and required somewhere in a debug client's handshake. Blank disables the check, which leaves the listener open to anyone who can reach the port.

reboot_listener_client_password.label: Reboot Listener Debug Password (reboot_listener_client_password)
reboot_listener_client_password.helperText: Blank = the stock debug password shipped with the template
reboot_listener_client_password.description: Handshake password for the debug-client protocol on the reboot listener's port - the part that makes the debugger's Reboot buttons work by changing only the port. Blank means the processor falls back to the stock DebugServer password, which is a constant in the template source, so set this AND a token for anything reachable off a trusted VLAN.

active_share_room.label: Share Room (active_share_room)
active_share_room.helperText: Swaps the projector pages for one grid of up to 13 screens
active_share_room.description: Drive the room's screens from a single grid page instead of the four projector detail pages. The screens are still PROJECTORDEVICE_n blocks counted by dev_projectors — what this changes is which manager runs them: the DisplayManager gives every slot one power button with a name under it (display_name_n) and polls one screen per 5s tick instead of all of them at once, which is what a wall of 8-13 panels needs. Slots 1-4 keep their detail page when they are projectors. Turn it on for a divisible/share space; leave it off and a normal room behaves exactly as before.

share_room_default_mode.label: Share Room Startup Mode (share_room_default_mode)

options.label: combined (every station shows the room's source)
individual (every station shows its own local input)

share_room_default_mode.helperText: Only read when a screen carries input_individual — see the projector tabs
share_room_default_mode.description: Which mode a share room comes up in. 'combined' (the default) puts every station on the room's source — the 'input' set on each PROJECTORDEVICE block; 'individual' puts each one on its own local input (input_individual). The panel's Combined/Individual toggle switches every station at once from then on. A room where no screen has an input_individual has no stations and ignores this.

display_name_*.helperText: Share room grid button label — \r starts a new line
display_name_*.description: Label under screen n's button on the share room grid page (display_name_1 ... display_name_13). Falls back to PROJECTORDEVICE_n's 'name' when it is absent, and then to 'Display n' / 'Projector n', so it only needs setting where the logger name is not what should be printed on the button. A \r puts the rest on a second line.
display_name_*.__comment: Share rooms only (active_share_room). Not in the template — absent means 'use the device name'.

input_sub_switcher.helperText: The MAIN switcher input the sub switcher feeds
input_sub_switcher.description: Switcher input the sub switcher is plugged into on the MAIN switcher — the input the main switcher parks on while the sub switcher does the source picking. Required whenever sub_switch_sources names anything: without it the processor logs an error and turns sub-switching off, because there is no input to park on. Nothing to do with sub_switch_CC, which is a separate feature.

sub_switch_sources.helperText: Comma-separated source names, e.g. "pc,hdmi,usb". Blank = off
sub_switch_sources.description: Sources that arrive through a SECOND switcher hanging off one input of the first (OCNL346's DTP T USW 333 feeding input 8 of an IN1608). For every source named here, the matching input_<name> is the SUB switcher's input number rather than the main one, and pressing that source drives both boxes: the sub switcher picks the source, the main switcher stays on input_sub_switcher. Names match the panel's own source names — pc, hdmi, usb, doc_cam and so on; an unrecognised name is logged and ignored. Blank or absent turns the whole feature off and every input_* means what it always did. Not the same as sub_switch_CC, which only diverts capture-card routing; the two can be used together.
sub_switch_sources.__comment: The processor also accepts a JSON list here; the comma string is what this app writes.

sub_switch_switcher.label: Sub Switcher Number (sub_switch_switcher)

options.label: 2 — SWITCHERDEVICE_2
3 — SWITCHERDEVICE_3

sub_switch_switcher.helperText: Which switcher block is the sub switcher (default 2)
sub_switch_switcher.description: Which switcher handler does the source picking for sub_switch_sources: SWITCHERDEVICE_2 or SWITCHERDEVICE_3. Defaults to 2. Only read when sub_switch_sources names at least one source, and the chosen block has to exist — check dev_switchers covers it.

__comment: THE TWO KINDS OF SHARE ROOM. 'active_share_room' turns one of them on
and 'share_room_type' picks which, because they answer the same
question ('which picture is on the screens?') with different hardware
and share nothing but the word:
display  a wall of panels on a distribution amp (OCNL346), switched
between the room's source and their own local input as a
room-wide combined/individual mode. The screens are
PROJECTORDEVICE_n blocks counted by dev_projectors, and
input_individual on a screen is what makes it a station.
This is DisplayManager, and it is the default.
nav      a ring of student stations on AV-over-IP (BSS122). Each
station is an encoder input and a decoder output on a
NAVigator, its display is a STATIONDEVICE_n block, and the
instructor can Share / Preview / Control any one of them.
This is NavShareManager, and every key below is read only
in this mode.
Setting dev_nav_switchers or dev_share_stations to 0 in the wizard
removes the keys that family owns (device_types 'systemKeys'), which
is why a normal teaching room carries none of this.

share_room_type.label: Share Room Type (share_room_type)

options.label: display — panels on a DA, combined/individual (DisplayManager)
nav — student stations over AV-over-IP (NavShareManager)

share_room_type.helperText: Only read while active_share_room is on. Absent = display
share_room_type.description: Which of the two share rooms this is — see the note above. 'display' is the processor's default when the key is absent, so an existing OCNL346-style room keeps working untouched; 'nav' swaps in the whole station page and needs a NAVDEVICE block, a STATIONDEVICE block per station, and the share_* keys below. Anything else is logged and treated as 'display'.

share_nav_device.description: Which NAVDEVICE_n block is the NAVigator the stations are tied on. Defaults to 1, and a value that is not a device number is logged and falls back to NAVDEVICE_1. Only matters in a room with more than one NAV stream manager.

input_station_*.helperText: NAV encoder input for station n's room feed
input_station_*.description: Encoder input carrying station n's normal picture — the room feed it shows when nothing is being shared. Read by NavShareManager when it ties a station onto the instructor's confidence monitor (Preview) or onto every screen (Share). NAV share rooms only.

input_station_*_laptop.helperText: The station's OWN laptop encoder input — blank means it has none
input_station_*_laptop.description: Encoder input carrying the laptop plugged in AT station n. A station without one can never be switched to 'HDMI' on the share page and its signal lamp stays dark, which is the correct behaviour for a station with no plate — so leave it blank rather than pointing it at something else.
input_station_*_laptop.__comment: Listed after input_station_* so the more specific pattern wins (patterns match in reverse file order).

output_station_*.helperText: NAV decoder output feeding station n's display
output_station_*.description: Decoder output the station n display hangs off. Everything the share page does to a station — putting the room on it, putting it back on its own picture, handing its USB over — lands on this output. NAV share rooms only.

share_station_*_name.helperText: Panel button text — defaults to "Station n"
share_station_*_name.description: What the share page calls station n. Only needs setting where the stations have real names (a pod letter, a table number) rather than being counted.

share_instructor_name.description: What the share page calls the instructor position. The instructor is a station on that page in every way except that it has no laptop input, no display of its own and no USB to take.

share_instructor_input.description: Encoder input carrying the instructor position — what Share sends to the room when 'Instructor' is picked, and what the confidence monitor goes back to when Preview is left (unless share_preview_idle_input says otherwise).

share_instructor_wireless_input.helperText: Optional — the encoder the wireless receiver arrives on
share_instructor_wireless_input.description: Encoder carrying the wireless receiver. Sharing 'Instructor' while the room is on its wireless source shares THIS instead, because the instructor position is showing wireless and that is a different encoder. Leave it blank in a room whose wireless does not reach the NAV.

share_room_outputs.description: The decoder outputs that follow the shared source — the room's projectors and the instructor monitor. These are what a station lands on when it is shared, and what share_stop_ties puts back when sharing stops.

share_stop_ties.description: What to re-tie on the share_room_outputs when sharing stops. Sharing displaces whatever the room was showing, and an instructor who stops sharing expects the room back on its source, not black — so this is the room's normal picture written down. Every output named in share_room_outputs should appear here.

share_stop_ties_wireless.helperText: Optional — the same pairs, for when the room is on wireless
share_stop_ties_wireless.description: share_stop_ties for a room whose selected source is wireless, which arrives on a different encoder. Optional: absent, the plain share_stop_ties are used and a wireless room comes back on the wrong input.

share_preview_output.helperText: Decoder output feeding the instructor's confidence monitor
share_preview_output.description: The output Preview mode puts a station on — the instructor sees that station and nobody else's screen changes. A room without this key has no Preview mode, and the processor says so in the log once rather than on every press.

share_preview_idle_input.description: What to put back on the preview output when Preview is left. Defaults to the instructor's own encoder, which is what the confidence monitor normally shows.

share_usb_device_output.helperText: The instructor's USB device number on the NAV
share_usb_device_output.description: USB device number the instructor's peripherals hang off. Control mode ties a station's USB — its touch overlay, mainly — to this, so the instructor can drive that station from the front of the room.

share_usb_station_offset.helperText: Station n's USB device is offset + n. Default 100
share_usb_station_offset.description: How a station's USB device number is derived from its station number: device = offset + n. The default 100 gives 101, 102, ... which is also what each station's USB is tied back to when the instructor releases Control.

share_audio_switcher.helperText: Optional — omit it and sharing makes no audio tie
share_audio_switcher.description: Which SWITCHERDEVICE_n carries room audio while a station is being shared. A station's audio only exists on the NAV, so it has to come back into the room through a switcher input — see share_audio_nav_input. Leave it blank in a room where sharing is video only.

share_audio_output.description: The output on share_audio_switcher that room audio is tied to while sharing. Normally the same output as output_audio.

share_audio_nav_input.helperText: That switcher's input carrying the NAVigator's audio return
share_audio_nav_input.description: The input on share_audio_switcher that the NAVigator's audio return is wired to. Room audio comes back through here whenever a station is being shared.

dev_nav_switchers.description: How many NAV stream managers (NAVigators) the room has. Sets how many NAVDEVICE_n blocks exist. Deliberately not counted in dev_switchers: a NAVigator is a matrix of encoders and decoders that only the share page knows how to tie, and the switcher pages would send it commands it does not answer. Dropping this to 0 also clears the room-wide share_* keys, since they configure nothing without a NAV behind them.

dev_share_stations.description: How many student stations a NAV share room has. Sets how many STATIONDEVICE_n blocks exist and how many station buttons the share page draws. Dropping it to 0 also clears the per-station input_station_*, output_station_* and share_station_* keys. Needs active_share_room on and share_room_type "nav" to mean anything.

METRICS_CONFIG.label: Metrics (Python Metric Tracking)
METRICS_CONFIG.__comment: Not a property - this names the METRICS_CONFIG group heading on the System tab. Its properties live under 'section_fields'.
METRICS_CONFIG.description: Metric tracking for the python side: the processor batches events (system start/stop, device connects, UI presses) and POSTs them to the ingest service. Converted rooms get it enabled with the bearer token already filled in.

ENVIRONMENT.label: Environment (Processor Runtime)
ENVIRONMENT.__comment: Not a property - this names the ENVIRONMENT group heading on the System tab. Its properties live under 'section_fields'.
ENVIRONMENT.description: Runtime switches for the processor itself. Every converted room gets this block with controlscript_profile set to 'pro'; traceback_allowed stays opt-in and is only here when the room's own file asked for it.

dev_cameras.description: How many cameras the room has. Sets how many CAMERADEVICE_n blocks exist (edit them on the Devices tabs) and how many camera controls the panel shows. The processor also uses it to decide whether to route a camera to the capture card at all.

dev_dsps.description: How many DSPs the room has. Sets how many DSPDEVICE_n blocks exist. Any count above 0 puts the room in 'DSP system' mode, where volume and mute go to the DSP's audio groups instead of the switcher's.

dev_media_ports.description: How many MediaPort USB interfaces the room has. Sets how many MEDIAPORTDEVICE_n blocks exist.

dev_power_controllers.description: How many power controllers (APC) the room has. Sets how many POWERDEVICE_n blocks exist. Dropping it to 0 also clears the power1_outlet_* names, since a room with no controller has no outlets to label.

dev_projectors.description: How many projectors/displays the room has. Sets how many PROJECTORDEVICE_n blocks exist, how many power buttons the panel shows, and how many output_proj_n outputs the processor routes and video-mutes.

dev_recorders.description: How many recorders (AV Bridge and the like) the room has. Sets how many RECORDERDEVICE_n blocks exist.

dev_relay_power.label: Relay Power Control (dev_relay_power)
dev_relay_power.description: Whether the room uses processor relay ports for power control (not a device count). Edited under Hardware Options in the Setup Wizard.

dev_screen_control.label: Screen Control Method (dev_screen_control)
dev_screen_control.description: How the projection screens are controlled: 'Relay' (processor relay ports), 'Serial' (direct RS-232), 'Serial over Ethernet', or 'Network' (not a device count). Edited under Hardware Options in the Setup Wizard.

dev_screens.description: How many projection screens the room has. Sets how many SCREENDEVICE_n blocks exist. How those screens are driven is dev_screen_control (relay ports, serial, or network).

dev_switchers.description: How many switchers the room has. Sets how many SWITCHERDEVICE_n blocks exist. Switcher 1 is the main matrix/scaler every route goes through; switchers 2 and 3 are the sub-switchers used for capture-card routing (sub_switch_CC) and Conference mode (conf_display_1 / conf_display_2).

dev_usb_switchers.description: How many USB switchers the room has. Sets how many USBDEVICE_n blocks exist — the device that hands the room's USB camera/mic over to the laptop or the room PC.

dev_wireless.description: How many wireless presentation devices (ShareLink, VIA) the room has. Sets how many WIRELESSDEVICE_n blocks exist; the wireless source button also needs input_wireless set.

gve_bldg.description: Building CODE for GVE (e.g. 'BSS' for Behavioral and Social Science), from buildings.json. The Setup Wizard stores the code here and generates gui_full_room_name from the full building name.

gve_room.description: Room number as GVE knows it (e.g. '103'). Paired with gve_bldg it identifies the room to GVE, and the two together name the backup files this app writes (BSS103_old_config.json).

gve_id_processor.description: GVE device ID for the processor itself, copied from GVE after the room is created there. Carried in the config as the room's inventory record — device connection statuses are reported under each device block's own gve_id.

gve_id_room_1.description: GVE ROOM ID, copied from GVE after the room is created there. This is the one GVE sends room events to: a SystemOn or SystemOff addressed to this ID starts or shuts down the room, so a wrong value means GVE cannot power the room.

gve_id_room_2.description: GVE room ID for the second room of a divisible/paired space. Set it to N/A in a single room.

gve_id_tlp_1.description: GVE device ID for the touch panel, copied from GVE. The processor reports the panel as Online under this ID at startup and whenever Force Online is pressed, so GVE shows the TLP as connected.

gve_ip.description: DNS name or IP of the GVE server the processor connects to (port 5555). Example: gve.csuchico.edu. Every device status, source change and power event the room reports goes here.

__comment: input_* / output_* are switcher CONNECTOR NUMBERS, written as strings.
Pressing a source on the panel reads input_<source> and ties that
input to output_audio, output_audio_ald and every output_proj_N.
A blank or missing value means the room does not have that source or
destination: the processor logs it and routes nothing, which is how a
room without (say) a Blu-ray is configured. The processor strips
non-digits from most output values, so '5B' reaches the switcher as 5.

input_aud_cam.description: Switcher input the audience camera is wired to. Routed to the second capture card (output_cc2) for the far end of a Zoom/Teams call. In a one-camera room, leave the camera you don't have blank — the panel keeps a single 'Camera' routing button and the processor falls back to whichever camera input IS set.

input_blu_ray.description: Switcher input the Blu-ray player is wired to. Only reachable when the sources list (gui_inputs) includes BluRay.

input_doc_cam.description: Switcher input the document camera is wired to. Only reachable when the sources list (gui_inputs) includes a Doc Cam.

input_dvd.description: Switcher input the DVD player is wired to. Only reachable when the sources list (gui_inputs) includes DVD.

input_hdmi.description: Switcher input for the room's HDMI connection — the laptop plate or cubby cable. Present on every sources layout.

input_inst_cam.description: Switcher input the instructor camera is wired to. Routed to the capture card (output_cc) for a Zoom/Teams call, and sent to LoopOut on switchers that have one (IN1806/IN1808, DTP2 CrossPoint 82). In a one-camera room the audience camera button falls back to this input.

input_pc.description: Switcher input the room PC is wired to — the input number to enter when the room has a PC. It is also the room's startup default: at power-on the processor ties it to program audio (output_audio), the ALD feed (output_audio_ald), the confidence monitor (output_monitor_1) and every projector output. Leave it blank in a room with no PC.

input_pc_extended.description: Switcher input carrying the PC's SECOND display output (extended desktop). Tied to output_monitor_2 at startup, so the lectern monitor can show a different picture from the projectors. Blank in a room whose PC has one output.

input_usb.description: Switcher input for the room's USB-C plate — or the VGA plate in an older room, which is what gui_usb_or_vga selects. The key name stays input_usb either way; only the panel label and this field's label change.

input_wireless.description: Switcher input the wireless presentation device (ShareLink, VIA) is wired to. Only reachable when the sources list (gui_inputs) includes Wireless.

output_audio.description: Switcher output feeding the room's program audio. Every source selection ties the chosen input here as an Audio-only tie (Audio/Video on a DTP2, which cannot break audio out), so this is the output the volume slider and program mute act on. On a DTP2 CrossPoint 82 the processor forces the audio breakaway to output 2 regardless of this value.

output_cc.description: Switcher output feeding the capture card / USB interface used for Zoom and Teams — what the far end sees. The instructor camera routes here by default; on a switcher with a LoopOut (IN1806/IN1808, DTP2 CrossPoint 82) the processor uses that instead of a matrix tie.

output_cc2.description: Switcher output feeding a SECOND capture card, used by the audience camera. Setting it is what gives the panel its CC2 routing row — a room without a second capture path leaves it blank.

output_monitor_1.description: Switcher output feeding the lectern / confidence monitor. The room PC (input_pc) is tied here at startup as a Video-only tie, so the monitor keeps showing the PC while the projectors follow the source buttons.

output_monitor_2.description: Switcher output feeding a second lectern monitor, tied to the PC's extended desktop (input_pc_extended) at startup. Blank in a room with one monitor.

output_proj_1.description: Switcher output feeding projector/display 1. Every source selection ties the chosen input here, and video mute is sent to this output. Non-digits are stripped by the processor, so '5B' (a DTP output's B connector) reaches the switcher as output 5. The literal string 'None' skips the mute for a display the switcher does not drive.

output_proj_2.description: Switcher output feeding projector/display 2 — see output_proj_1. Only read while dev_projectors is 2 or more.

output_proj_3.description: Switcher output feeding projector/display 3 — see output_proj_1. Only read while dev_projectors is 3 or more.

output_proj_4.description: Switcher output feeding projector/display 4 — see output_proj_1. Only read while dev_projectors is 4.

conf_display_1.helperText: An INPUT on the conference switcher (Switcher 3), not an output
conf_display_1.description: Input number the conference switcher (SWITCHERDEVICE_3) is set to when 'Display 1' is pressed on the Conference routing page — the codec's first display feed. Read only while gui_routing_mode is Conference.

conf_display_2.helperText: An INPUT on the conference switcher (Switcher 3), not an output
conf_display_2.description: Input number the conference switcher (SWITCHERDEVICE_3) is set to when 'Display 2' is pressed on the Conference routing page — the codec's second display feed. Read only while gui_routing_mode is Conference.

gui_routing_mode.description: How the room's displays are driven. 'Normal': every display follows the selected source. 'Extended': displays 2 and 4 show the PC's extended desktop (input_pc_extended) while 1 and 3 follow the source, and the routing pages switch to their Extended layouts. 'Conference': the room is built around a codec — the Conference routing page appears and drives the conference switcher with conf_display_1 / conf_display_2, and the camera pages change to match.

options.label: Menu Tabs: 2 - Camera & Devices
Menu Tabs: 2 - Mic & Devices
Menu Tabs: 3 - Camera, Mic, & Devices
Menu Tabs: 3 - Cameras & Devices
Menu Tabs: 4 - Cameras, Mic, & Devices
Menu Tabs: 2 - Camera & Devices (subs the Camera2Handler — no instructor camera)

gui_tab.description: Which menu tabs the panel shows down the side of the main page, so a room only carries the controls it has: cameras, microphone, devices, or a combination. Pick the entry matching the room's hardware — the count in each option is how many tabs appear. 'Conference' is the 2-tab camera layout for a codec room and also substitutes the second camera handler, so there is no instructor camera.

gui_routing_available.description: Whether the panel offers the routing pages — the video matrix button and the per-destination source picking. 'No' leaves the room on the plain source buttons, which is what most teaching rooms want; 'Yes' suits a room where someone needs to send different sources to different displays.

gui_inputs.label: Sources & Routing Config (gui_inputs + gui_tab_type)

4 Sources: PC, HDMI, Doc Cam, & USB

gui_inputs.description: Used in conjunction with gui_tab_type to set the sources in the room for the source and routing pages.

gui_tab_type.__comment: Written by the gui_inputs combo dropdown; never shown directly.
gui_tab_type.description: Used in conjunction with gui_inputs to set the sources. (Examples: 3_WL, 4_DOC_USB, 6_DOC_DVD_VGA_WL, etc).

options.label: Yes (Single Mic w/ Ducking)
No (Single Mic w/ Mute)
Ceiling (Voicelift & Mute)

gui_mic_mix.description: Specify the Microphone sub page: 'Yes' (Single Mic w/ Ducking), 'No' (Single Mic w/ Mute), 'Ceiling' (Ceiling Mic w/ Voicelift).

gui_preset_name_aud_*.helperText: Panel button text — \r starts a new line
gui_preset_name_aud_*.description: Button text for the audience camera's stored presets 1-4 (the camera holds the actual positions; this only names the buttons). Name them for what the shot is — 'Left', 'Wide', 'Whiteboard'. A \r puts the rest on a second line, which is how a two-word name fits the button.
gui_preset_name_aud_*.__comment: One wildcard entry covers gui_preset_name_aud_1 through _4.

gui_preset_name_inst_*.helperText: Panel button text — \r starts a new line
gui_preset_name_inst_*.description: Button text for the instructor camera's stored presets 1-4 (the camera holds the actual positions; this only names the buttons). Name them for what the shot is — 'Lectern', 'Wide', 'Whiteboard'. A \r puts the rest on a second line, which is how a two-word name fits the button.
gui_preset_name_inst_*.__comment: One wildcard entry covers gui_preset_name_inst_1 through _4.

gui_full_room_name.description: Room name printed across the panel's pages, e.g. 'Butte Hall 103'. Free text for people in the room to read — the Setup Wizard fills it in from the building name and room number, unlike gve_bldg/gve_room which are the codes GVE matches on.

mic_max_volume.description: Loudest the microphone slider can reach, in dB as the DSP/switcher reads it (processor default 0). With mic_min_volume it defines the range the panel's mic slider maps onto — so 0 to -10 means a full slider is 0 dB and the bottom is -10 dB, not 'off'.
mic_max_volume.helperText: dB at the top of the mic slider (default 0)

mic_min_volume.description: Quietest the microphone slider can reach, in dB (processor default -10). Raise it (e.g. -6) in a room where the bottom of the slider still needs to be audible; lower it for finer control over a wider range.
mic_min_volume.helperText: dB at the bottom of the mic slider (default -10)

switch_max_volume.description: Loudest the program volume slider can reach, in dB (processor default 0). With switch_min_volume it defines the range the panel's program slider maps onto, whether the level lands on the switcher or the DSP.
switch_max_volume.helperText: dB at the top of the program slider (default 0)

switch_min_volume.description: Quietest the program volume slider can reach, in dB (processor default -40). This is the floor a user can drag to, not a mute — muting is a separate command.
switch_min_volume.helperText: dB at the bottom of the program slider (default -40)

teams_webhook.description: Power Automate webhook URL the room posts its Teams notifications to (device offline, errors). Only used while active_notifications is true; blank it and the room reports nothing.

sub_switch_CC.helperText: The string "true" turns it on — anything else is off
sub_switch_CC.description: Route the capture-card destinations through the SECONDARY switchers instead of the main one: CC1 goes to Switcher 2 and CC2 to Switcher 3, each set by input number rather than a matrix tie. For a room where the capture feeds hang off their own small switcher. Leave it null/false and CC routing stays on switcher 1.

tv_videomute.description: On a DTP2 CrossPoint 82 only: when video mute is pressed, DON'T mute switcher output 1 — the display on that output is muted by its own command instead, which keeps the HDBaseT link to the TV alive. Added for Arts 208; leave it 'No' in a room that doesn't need the exception (the other outputs mute normally either way).

power1_outlet_*.description: Set the GUI names for the power controller (APC). 23 character limitation.
power1_outlet_*.__comment: One wildcard entry covers power1_outlet_1 through power1_outlet_8.

power1_outlet_*_supports_reboot.description: Whether this outlet's hardware can power-cycle on command. Optional — a room without the key behaves as before. Set false for an outlet that must only be switched on or off (a screen relay, a device that dislikes a hard cycle).
power1_outlet_*_supports_reboot.helperText: Optional. Leave unset for rooms that don't use reboot control.
power1_outlet_*_supports_reboot.__comment: Listed after the generic power1_outlet_* entry: patterns are matched in reverse file order, so the more specific one wins.

power1_outlet_*_reboot_only.description: Whether reboot is the ONLY action this outlet offers — the GUI hides plain on/off for it. Optional; needs power1_outlet_N_supports_reboot to be true to mean anything.
power1_outlet_*_reboot_only.helperText: Optional. Reboot is the only action offered for this outlet.
power1_outlet_*_reboot_only.__comment: Listed after the generic power1_outlet_* entry: patterns are matched in reverse file order, so the more specific one wins.

relay_port_*.description: Relay port on the processor used for screen control (e.g. RLY1). _up raises the screen, _down lowers it, _stop halts travel.

group_*.description: Audio group number on the switcher/DSP. Set these in DSP Configurator / PCS, or the third-party device's software (e.g. Yamaha MTX Editor).
group_*.__comment: Wildcard fallback: exact group_ entries above still win where defined.

auto_reconnect.description: Automatically re-establish the connection to the device (e.g. ShareLink) if it drops.

startup_watchdog_stage.description: Top-level counter used by the processor's startup watchdog to track boot progress/retries. Managed by the running system - normally leave at 0.
